category_title: Underachieving students in difficult PE contexts who alternate between task involvement and ephemeral off-task behaviors
minimal_context: The student is at a gymnastics workshop station in a PE class, using an instruction card to practice somersaults and jumps with a small group.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please look at the instruction cards at this station and start practicing your somersaults and jumps. Make sure to manage your repetitions.

STUDENT: Here, I arrive at the activity, quickly read the sheet to go through the various exercises. Here, I want to check if the exercises are hard. (Executes them one by one, slowly and precisely)

TUTOR: Keep practicing the exercises on the sheet.

STUDENT: Well, I try my best and then I practice this somersault, the hardest! (Makes a correct jump, puts up the equipment, and waits idly)

TUTOR: It is time for your next repetition.

STUDENT: (Chats with friends, gives a kick to a mat, and begins wandering about the gym) I work a bit but in the end it's boring to do the same thing over and over again, so I have a laugh with my mates. It's no big deal, and after that I work as well.

options.A: Move to the mat and physically guide the student into a starting position for the somersault, kneeling by their feet and grabbing their hands.
options.B: Validate the correct jump ("you're absolutely one hundred percent right") but immediately follow up with "But how did you know that?" to prompt a conceptual explanation.
options.C: Play an audio recording of the instruction card for the group, instead of having the student read the text for the gymnastics exercises.
options.D: Pretend not to see the minor, non-disruptive deviant acts (like kicking the mat or wandering) during the gymnastics activity at the station.
